text:
mina: Heads up — saw a reproducible decode jitter when we enable FP8 KV with the new dithered calibration on long-context runs (8k). Not a full regression but token-level probability wobble causing occasional token flips.

arjun: Can you paste a short repro and perf snapshot?

mina: Repro (quick):
```
# repro (local perf VM)
run_profile --model llama2-13b --kv-quant fp8-dither --calib-samples 2048 --batch 1 --seqlen 8192 --steps 50
```
Output summary (truncated):
```
config: fp8-dither, calib=2048
mem: peak_gpu=10.4GB (vs 25.8GB fp32)
latency: p50=24ms p95=48ms p99=120ms
decode-jitter-rate=0.8% (token flips on greedy vs. non-dithered baseline)
kv-cache-hit-rate ~99.7%
```

leah: Interesting — memory improvement looks great. 0.8% token flip feels small but could be visible for some chats. Did you check with deterministic seeds?

mina: Yes, deterministic seed reduces nondeterminism but the flip remains in a subset of prompts (mostly low-entropy prefix transitions). Hypothesis: quantization dither + kernel rounding during cache writes produces small probability perturbations that get amplified by softmax in next-step decoding.

sam: Any kernel switch logs around the jitter windows? We recently enabled opportunistic INT8->FP8 kernel switching for smaller batches.

mina: I attached a short log extract (copied):
```
[12:02:11.103] kernel_select: chosen=fp8_kv_smallseq (latency_est=19ms)
[12:02:11.104] kv_store: quantize=dithered_fp8, commit_bytes=12288
[12:02:11.125] kernel_switch: fallback=int8_kv (hysteresis not met)
[12:02:11.126] decode_step(42): token: "the" prob=0.121->0.117 (baseline 0.119)
```

arjun: Kernel flip during a single request is bad — that could explain mid-request changes. We should avoid switching kernels while a request is in-flight; there is already a per-request sticky flag but maybe it wasn't honored for the new fp8 path.

leah: Also calibration sample size might be insufficient. 2048 samples for some attention heads is borderline. Try 8192 or change sampling distribution (more long-seq examples).

sam: Quick A/B numbers from my side running 8192 calib samples + sticky per-request kernel:
```
8192 samples + sticky: p50=26ms p95=52ms p99=110ms, token flips=0.12%
512 samples: p50=22ms p95=46ms, token flips=1.7%
```
So calibration helps a lot but adds a few ms. Tradeoff: quality vs latency.

mina: Agreed. Another mitigation: add small hysteresis window for kernel switching (>3ms estimated delta) and prefer in-request stickiness. Also consider deterministic quant rounding (no dither) for low-entropy prefix routes while keeping dither for general traffic.

arjun: We should also profile KV write encoding variance. If the quant commit bytes vary across kernel implementations, that could change layout/padding and slightly alter numerical ops. Can someone run a byte-exact dump of KV writes across kernels?

leah: I'll run dump for 20 requests and diff the binary blobs. If we see bit-level differences from same fp values that indicates different rounding strategies.

mina: Action items: 1) leah run KV-write diffs (owner: leah) 2) eng-runtime create a short patch to enforce per-request sticky kernel for FP8 path and add hysteresis (owner: arjun) 3) perf team run calibs at 2048/8192 distribution and produce sampled token-flip heatmap (owner: sam).

sam: I'll also generate a small qual eval set (50 prompts with low-entropy endings) to quantify end-user impact.

arjun: Timeline? Can we have quick patches + CI calibs by EOD tomorrow?

leah: I can share KV diffs by EOD.

mina: I'll run the 8192 calibs overnight and post full decode traces in this thread.

ops-bot: Deploy window reminder — avoid kernel switches in prod rollout between 02:00-04:00 UTC to make tracing easier. :warning:

sam: One more note — we saw similar behavior months ago with int4 hybrid cache where rounding noise accumulated. That time we mitigated with additive small-scale smoothing of logits before argmax (tiny temp=1e-6). Could try that as a lightweight stopgap.

mina: Good suggestion. Try smoothing only for identified low-entropy suffixes to avoid changing general behavior.

arjun: Ok let's reconvene tomorrow after diffs + calibs. If leah/sam confirm bit-level nondeterminism + calibration fixes reduce flips to <0.2% we can plan a staged roll.

mina: Thanks all. I'll drop the full trace files (gz) here when ready.
